_about: How names and recurring terms are written in this language. Every translation follows this file, so a name is always spelled the same way. Names are written by sound, never translated (the author's rule). The spellings here are first versions based on the written names: the author's own pronunciation is recorded in Legacy/Behind The Scenes/World Lore/Word Pronunciation/Unique Words Pronounciation.wav, so correct any spelling here and later translations will follow it. Add new names the first time they are translated.
rule: Story names stay exactly as in English, as in Portuguese, Spanish, Malay, German, Vietnamese and Italian. That includes coined world terms written as names: creatures, plants, items, nari gels, spells, factions, guilds, places, ranks and coins (Wood People, Sand Worms, Fost Stone, Nari Refresher, Red Winga, Sapphire, Pearl). Plain words around them are translated into French and follow French word order (gel nari, pierres nari, bombes nari, interface Darfaries, aventurier Sapphire). Kingdoms read 'Royaume de Sanbi', guards 'gardes de Forway'. The currency balls is 'boules' (singular 'boule'), which keeps the slang double meaning; the rank follows it (boule sapphire, boules pearl). The unit timehunk stays as is. The reader is addressed as 'tu' everywhere, matching the author's casual voice; profanity is kept. Dates put the day first: '994 A.G. Adrian 6th' becomes '6 Adrian 994 A.G.' (the 1st is '1er'); with a weekday, 'Gannday 14 Paulin 1039 A.G.'. Gregorian dates read '1er juin 2020'. French typography: a narrow no-break space (U+202F) before ! ? ; : and inside « », added outside HTML tags and URLs. Category labels shared between pages use forms that fit any gender: Pacifiques, Hostiles, Sur la défensive. 'Sanbi shit!' (the Sanbi oath) is always 'Vieille âme de Sanbi !' ('Old Sanbi soul!'), the author's rule; 'Sanbi shit out of luck' becomes 'Tu n'auras plus que la poisse, vieille âme de Sanbi !'. France French spelling.
